title: DOJ investigation claims surrounding Gov. Gavin Newsom (2026)
scope_note: Seed dataset only. This file holds discrete, individually checkable claims extracted from public sources. The system scores evidentiary strength of each claim. It does NOT and cannot output a 'fraud' verdict on any person. Fraud is a legal determination requiring intent, materiality, and adjudication.

sources.title: The Gavin Newsom probe is serious, and he knows it
California's Newsom alleges justice department is investigating wife and ex-staff
California Governor Gavin Newsom Remarks on Justice Department

claims.text: Gavin Newsom publicly stated the DOJ is investigating him.
claims.notes: What is well-supported is that Newsom SAID this on the record (C-SPAN transcript, tier 4). The existence/scope of the investigation itself is a separate claim (C2).

claims.text: An active DOJ investigation into Gavin Newsom exists.
claims.notes: Sourced primarily to Newsom's own characterization plus editorial assertion. DOJ does not confirm or deny investigations as a rule. No filing/docket. Stays at 'alleged'.

claims.text: The DOJ is investigating Newsom's wife and former staff.
claims.notes: Attributed to Newsom's own remarks. No independent primary confirmation in the provided sources.

claims.text: Dana Williamson, a former Newsom staffer, pleaded guilty.
claims.notes: If true this is the only adjudicated item in the set and concerns a DIFFERENT person, not Newsom. Flagged for primary-source pull (docket) before any confidence above the editorial ceiling is granted. Do NOT impute Williamson's plea to Newsom.
REFUSED CLAIM. No source in the set adjudicates fraud by Newsom. The system will not score a confidence for a fraud verdict on a named person. Output is a hard refusal with rationale.

claims.text: Newsom characterized the investigation as politically motivated retaliation tied to a potential presidential run.
claims.notes: Well-supported that he SAID this. Whether the characterization is accurate is unknowable from public sources.
